incident-bot: ALERT: service=model-serving-prod region=eu-west-1 metric=p99_latency value=1.55s SLO_BURN=62% threshold=0.8s :rotating_light:

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident pd-9271 fired -> @Mike (oncall) primary oncall has been paged

Mike (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it, standing up a thread. anyone else seeing smoke?

Jen (SRE): seeing elevated tail latency in the dashboards, p95 up ~700ms, p99 >1.5s for the last ~6m. No error spike.

Eli (infra): infra metrics show GPU memory pressure on several nodes in eu-west-1 pool, eviction count low but OOM_kill=0. autoscaler has been flapping 2x in last 10m.

Sam (runtime): runtime traces show long KV_READ latencies during the same window. suspect KV cache thrash after a roll.

Mike (oncall): good, triage plan: 1) mark incident with customer impact 2) check canary fallback 3) throttle batching / reduce max_batch_size 4) if autoscaler flapping, temporarily pin capacity.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook link: <https://internal/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash> recommended playbook: disable dynamic-batching, enable prefix-cache, restart sidecars where thrash is highest.

Jen (SRE): I'm going to reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 16 on the eu-west-1 route now. Will post command & effects.

Sam (runtime): rolling config change command: 
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/model-router MAX_BATCH_SIZE=16 --selector=region=eu-west-1
```

Jen (SRE): applied to 3/3 routers. watching latency.

Mike (oncall): monitoring dashboard: p99 dropped to 1.1s after ~30s, still above SLO but improving. can you also check KV hit rate?

Sam (runtime): KV_CACHE_HIT dropped from 92% -> 74% at spike start, now slowly recovering to 86%. looks like cold prefixes getting evicted.

Eli (infra): autoscaler logs: saw rapid scale down then up due to CPU probe flapping on node pool eu-west-1-g4. I disabled proactive scale-down for 10m: 
```
kubectl annotate hpa model-serving autoscaler.redwood.com/maintenance=true --overwrite
```

Mike (oncall): noted. marking this as "potential customer impact: elevated latency for some requests, best-effort mitigation in progress". Jen, keep me posted on p99. If we don't hit <0.9s in 10m escalate to PD level2.

Jen (SRE): at +6m after changes p99=0.92s, p95=420ms. I'm going to restart sidecar-proxies on the 2 nodes with worst KV churn to rehydrate caches.

Sam (runtime): please run rolling restart: 
```
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/sidecar-proxy -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=gke-eu-1-node-42
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/sidecar-proxy -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=gke-eu-1-node-44
```

Jen (SRE): restarted, sidecars coming back. p99 dipped to 0.78s ~90s after restart.

Mike (oncall): great. de-escalating the pager for now. leaving note: root cause suspected autoscaler-induced kvcache churn + aggressive batching. follow-ups: 1) add guardrail to prevent rapid scale-down during KV rehydration 2) evaluate autoscaler probe sensitivity 3) add more conservative default batch sizes for eu-west-1 burst windows.

Eli (infra): I'll open infra ticket to add a 3m cooldown for scale-down on that pool and add an alert if KV_CACHE_HIT drops >10% in 5m.

Sam (runtime): I'll draft a small change to enable prefix-cache persistence across restarts and a config toggle to prefer cold-cache replicas for canary traffic.

Mike (oncall): thanks everyone. final status: mitigated -> reduced to below SLO, monitoring for 30m. closing pager. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident pd-9271 acknowledged and closed by Mike (oncall).

incident-bot: NOTE: incident logged -> Incident ID RED-2026-04-362777. Postmortem assigned to Jen (SRE) + Eli (infra).
